title: Harnessing omics data for drug discovery and development in ovarian aging.
authors: Zhang, Fengyu; Zhu, Ming; Chen, Yi; Wang, Guiquan; Yang, Haiyan; Lu, Xinmei; Li, Yan; Chang, Hsun-Ming; Wu, Yang; Ma, Yunlong; Yuan, Shuai; Zhu, Wencheng; Dong, Xi; Zhao, Yue; Yu, Yang; Wang, Jia; Mu, Liangshan
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦卵巢衰老的多组学数据与药物靶点发现，虽提及转录因子FOXP1和AI，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ovarian aging occurs earlier than the aging of many other organs and has a lasting impact on women's overall health and well-being. However, effective interventions to slow ovarian aging remain limited, primarily due to an incomplete understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms and drug targets. Recent advances in omics data resources, combined with innovative computational tools, are offering deeper insight into the molecular complexities of ovarian aging, paving the way for new opportunities in drug discovery and development. OBJECTIVE AND RATIONALE: This review aims to synthesize the expanding multi-omics data, spanning genome, transcriptome, proteome, metabolome, and microbiome, related to ovarian aging, from both tissue-level and single-cell perspectives. We will specially explore how the analysis of these emerging omics datasets can be leveraged to identify novel drug targets and guide therapeutic strategies for slowing and reversing ovarian aging. SEARCH METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search in the PubMed database using a range of relevant keywords: ovarian aging, age at natural menopause, premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), diminished ovarian reserve (DOR), genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, DNA methylation, RNA modification, histone modification, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, microbiome, single-cell, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), whole-exome sequencing, phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS), Mendelian randomization (MR), epigenetic target, drug target, machine learning, artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning, and multi-omics. The search was restricted to English-language articles published up to September 2024. OUTCOMES: Multi-omics studies have uncovered key mechanisms driving ovarian aging, including DNA damage and repair deficiencies, inflammatory and immune responses, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell death. By integrating multi-omics data, researchers can identify critical regulatory factors and mechanisms across various biological levels, leading to the discovery of potential drug targets. Notable examples include genetic targets such as BRCA2 and TERT, epigenetic targets like Tet and FTO, metabolic targets such as sirtuins and CD38+, protein targets like BIN2 and PDGF-BB, and transcription factors such as FOXP1. WIDER IMPLICATIONS: The advent of cutting-edge omics technologies, especially single-cell technologies and spatial transcriptomics, has provided valuable insights for guiding treatment decisions and has become a powerful tool in drug discovery aimed at mitigating or reversing ovarian aging. As technology advances, the integration of single-cell multi-omics data with AI models holds the potential to more accurately predict candidate drug targets. This convergence offers promising new avenues for personalized medicine and precision therapies, paving the way for tailored interventions in ovarian aging. REGISTRATION NUMBER: Not applicable.
abstract_zh: 背景：卵巢衰老的发生早于许多其他器官的衰老，并对女性的整体健康和福祉产生持久影响。然而，减缓卵巢衰老的有效干预措施仍然有限，主要原因是对其潜在分子机制和药物靶点的理解尚不完整。近年来，组学数据资源的进展，结合创新的计算工具，正在为卵巢衰老的分子复杂性提供更深入的见解，为药物发现和开发开辟新的机遇。目的与理由：本综述旨在综合与卵巢衰老相关的不断扩展的多组学数据，涵盖基因组、转录组、蛋白质组、代谢组和微生物组，从组织水平和单细胞视角进行探讨。我们将特别探索如何利用这些新兴组学数据集的分析来识别新的药物靶点，并指导减缓及逆转卵巢衰老的治疗策略。检索方法：我们在PubMed数据库中使用一系列相关关键词进行了全面文献检索：卵巢衰老、自然绝经年龄、早发性卵巢功能不全（POI）、卵巢储备功能减退（DOR）、基因组学、转录组学、表观基因组学、DNA甲基化、RNA修饰、组蛋白修饰、蛋白质组学、代谢组学、脂质组学、微生物组、单细胞、全基因组关联研究（GWAS）、全外显子组测序、表型组关联研究（PheWAS）、孟德尔随机化（MR）、表观遗传靶点、药物靶点、机器学习、人工智能（AI）、深度学习和多组学。检索限制为截至2024年9月发表的英文文章。结果：多组学研究已揭示驱动卵巢衰老的关键机制，包括DNA损伤与修复缺陷、炎症和免疫反应、线粒体功能障碍以及细胞死亡。通过整合多组学数据，研究人员可以识别跨多个生物水平的关键调控因子和机制，从而发现潜在的药物靶点。显著例子包括遗传靶点如BRCA2和TERT，表观遗传靶点如Tet和FTO，代谢靶点如sirtuins和CD38+，蛋白质靶点如BIN2和PDGF-BB，以及转录因子如FOXP1。更广泛影响：尖端组学技术的出现，尤其是单细胞技术和空间转录组学，为指导治疗决策提供了宝贵见解，并已成为旨在缓解或逆转卵巢衰老的药物发现中的强大工具。随着技术的进步，单细胞多组学数据与AI模型的整合有望更准确地预测候选药物靶点。这种融合为个性化医疗和精准治疗提供了有前景的新途径，为卵巢衰老的定制干预铺平了道路。注册号：不适用。
